title: Cycle Pulse: staffing resilience and mid-cycle scope elasticity
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Mid-cycle surprises (unplanned incidents, hiring delays, or unexpected cross-team work) are forcing ad-hoc scope cuts and manual reallocation. This causes churn, missed OKRs, and uneven engineer load.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'Cycle Pulse' protocol and tooling to continuously surface capacity signals, automate common scope-trimming decisions, and provide a clear playbook for rapid, low-friction mid-cycle adjustments. The outcome should reduce decision time for scope cuts by >=50% and improve team satisfaction during mid-cycle rebalances.

Scope: Protocol, dashboard signals, templated triage steps, a small automation rule engine (opt-in), and playbook docs. This ticket delivers the PM product spec, roll-out plan, and initial automation rules. Engineering work to implement signals and dashboards will be tracked as dependent ENG tickets. Design artifacts link to the UI mockups for the dashboard and triage flow.
acceptance_criteria: A public Cycle Pulse page exists in Console with: current staffed FTE per initiative, active blockers, and a health badge (green/amber/red)
A set of 3 templated scope-cut options per initiative (defer, shrink, replace) with default engineering effort estimates and impact notes
Two automated triggers implemented (unplanned incident > 8 hours affecting SLA; sustained >20% capacity drop across an initiative for 3 days) that create an agenda item and notify owners
Runbook and playbook published in Confluence with decision matrix and escalation path
Pilot conducted with 2 product teams over one cycle and feedback captured (NPS-style + qualitative notes)

decision_log: Prefer lightweight opt-in automation to avoid noisy alerts and to respect team autonomy.
Health badge thresholds: Green >= 90% capacity, Amber 70-90%, Red < 70% (configurable per initiative)
Three default scope-cut templates to standardize tradeoffs and speed decisions: Defer (low risk), Shrink (medium risk), Replace with cross-team cheaper alternative (high coordination).
risks_mitigation: Risk: Metrics pipeline lag could make signals stale -> Mitigation: mark timestamp, show staleness warning, and plan a 'near-real-time' metrics stream as follow-up
Risk: Teams opt out due to perceived micromanagement -> Mitigation: clearly communicate opt-in, local ownership, and provide value in reduced meeting load
Risk: Automation false positives -> Mitigation: require owner confirmation before any automatic scope change; first three months automation runs in audit-only mode
notes_for_review: Please review the acceptance criteria and suggest one additional low-friction scope-removal template if helpful.
Design: confirm that the triage modal can be rendered in the existing Console layout without a major refactor.
